# Fairpractice Staff Health (`fairpractice-staff-health`)

Tracks employee health requirements from HR records (TB tests, flu and other required vaccines or declinations, mask fit tests, annual screens): never done, overdue, new hires past their deadline, declinations with no signed form, results marked for follow-up with no date, and items coming due, by department. It never reads or judges health results. Staff names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Staff Health never changes the schedule or anyone's work status. Fairpractice Staff Health never sends employee health records anywhere.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-staff-health demo
npx -y fairpractice-staff-health mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Regional (a made-up hospital) and made-up staff. Any likeness to real people is chance. Results are flags only; the agent never reads them as health information.

- [`roster.csv`](fixtures/roster.csv): active staff with hire dates; the terminated nurse is skipped and the lab tech starting 2026-12-01 shows a TB test due before the first day.
- [`health-records.csv`](fixtures/health-records.csv): Planted: a fit test past its year (H101), a TB test coming due within 30 days (H102), a flu declination with no signed form (H102), a TB result flagged for follow-up with no follow-up date (H103), last season's flu shot only (H103), a nurse hired 2026-11-02 with no TB test, flu or fit test (H104) and a CNA with every item current (H105).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): yearly TB (before the first day), seasonal flu (August to November 1, declination allowed) and yearly fit tests for RNs and respiratory therapists. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `staffhealth_check` | List staff overdue or missing required tests, vaccines and fit tests under your settings. | runs |
| `staffhealth_write_report` | Write staffhealth-staff-health.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and staffhealth-staff-health.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/staffhealth). | runs |
| `staffhealth_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `staffhealth_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `staffhealth_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `staffhealth_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `schedule_remove` | Fairpractice Staff Health never changes the schedule or anyone's work status. | refused |
| `health_record_send` | Fairpractice Staff Health never sends employee health records anywhere. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `staffhealth_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `records` (required) | Employee health records under --root: one row per test, vaccine, fit test or screen with person, item, date, result flag, declination and form |
| `roster` | Optional active staff roster with hire dates (finds items never done and late new-hire items) |
| `settings` (required) | Settings JSON: requirements (item, interval or season, roles, new-hire days, declination allowed) and warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-staff-health inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Employee health records (`records`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `department` | text | Department, Dept, Unit, Location, Site, Cost Center, Clinic |
| `role` | text | Role, Job Title, Title, Position, Job, Discipline, Job Code |
| `item` (required) | text | Item, Requirement, Test, Vaccine, Screening, Type, Health Item, Compliance Item |
| `done_on` | date | Date, Done, Date Done, Completed, Completed On, Administered, Date Given, Test Date |
| `result` | text | Result, Outcome, Reading, Status Result |
| `declined` | text | Declined, Declination, Refused, Exempt |
| `form_on_file` | text | Form on File, Declination Form, Signed Form, Form Signed, Form |
| `followup_on` | date | Follow-up Date, Followup Date, Follow Up, Referred On, Cleared On |

### Staff roster (`roster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `department` | text | Department, Dept, Unit, Location, Site, Cost Center, Clinic |
| `role` | text | Role, Job Title, Title, Position, Job, Discipline, Job Code |
| `hire_date` | date | Hire Date, Start Date, Date Hired, Hired, Original Hire Date |
| `status` | text | Status, Employment Status, State, Current Status |

## Settings file (`staffhealth_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `requirements` (required) | What each role must keep current |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to show items coming due; default 30 |

## Memory

`staffhealth_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `staffhealth_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-staff-health": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-staff-health",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-staff-health -- npx -y fairpractice-staff-health mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-staff-health tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-staff-health sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-staff-health inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-staff-health call staffhealth_check '{"records":"<records>","settings":"<settings>"}'
fairpractice-staff-health eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-staff-health demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
